Resumption is refused when the write-budget guard was absent, failed, or when the last event is incomplete.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The write-budget guard was not implemented or was bypassed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"An event write was initiated with insufficient tokens and partially persisted.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The replay function is non-deterministic (depends on wall-clock time, external APIs, or randomness not captured in the log).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log format is not self-describing, so replay cannot determine where the last complete event ends.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"External side effects (network calls, file writes) occurred during the original run and cannot be re-derived on replay.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In event sourcing, the log IS the state. A write-budget guard checks remaining tokens before beginning an event write and halts cleanly if insufficient, guaranteeing no partial writes. Replay reconstructs state deterministically from the complete log. Resumption simply continues from the replayed state, appending with the next identity. The guard is the causal mechanism that makes clean halts guaranteed rather than accidental.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
